{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nv-c","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"dc7b32bfb789b140c9c67204c09eb4e05409994ced67fd4cc27d7dcf6aee6d91","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nv-class-c:lineage:6","source_registry_sha256":"3e184808e042e052d0c78d0dff47c50b34a56560f428649c492afe10bc7ba712","source_liveness_sha256":"0dfbf3aa4b4798b88d69252e076642b5f0a38751c5010711fbce93c8a7d6e292"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Young-driver and class confusables with licensing continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: practice-hour paths, permit supervision, the three six-month rules, towing classes, ID card versus license, and continuation facts on endorsements, motorcycles, designations, donation and fees","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: practice-hour paths, permit supervision, the three six-month rules, towing classes, ID card versus license, and continuation facts on endorsements, motorcycles, designations, donation and fees
Confusable pairs from the young-driver, permit and class rules, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block. Motorcycle and commercial blocks are scope-noted continuation only.

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A01
A low alcohol reading between 0.02% and 0.08% already costs a young driver a 185-day revocation, while a first DUI offense puts the young driver under the full adult penalties. [A01]
Why it matters: group young-driver penalties; confusable low-level alcohol versus DUI offense.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A01
A student previously declared a habitual truant under NRS 392.144 whose license or permit was suspended must bring a new DMV-301 showing current attendance before driving privileges are reinstated. [A01]
Why it matters: group school attendance; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A02
The standard path is 50 supervised hours with 10 at night; the remote path for teens beyond 30 miles of a school and without internet access is 100 hours with 10 in the dark. [A02]
Why it matters: group practice hours; confusable fifty versus one hundred hours.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A02
For a motorcycle license on the remote path, all 100 practice hours must be driven in daylight only. [A02]
Why it matters: group practice hours; scope note motorcycle only.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A03
A Class C permit supervisor sits in the seat beside you, while a motorcycle or moped permit supervisor must ride a motorcycle within direct sight and may not be in a car or truck. [A03]
Why it matters: group permits; confusable car versus motorcycle supervision.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A03
A Class M or M-Z permit holder rides in daylight only, carries no passengers and stays off limited-access highways and freeways. [A03]
Why it matters: group permits; scope note motorcycle and moped only.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A03
Three different six-month rules apply to Nevada teens: hold the permit at least six months, carry no non-family passengers under 18 for the first six months of licensed driving, and stay crash- and conviction-free for six months before licensing. [A03]
Why it matters: group teen limits; confusable three six-month rules.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A04
Class A covers combinations rated over 26,000 pounds GCWR with a trailer over 10,000 pounds, Class B covers a single vehicle over 26,000 pounds GVWR that may tow under 10,000 pounds, and Class M covers motorcycles and mopeds. [A04]
Why it matters: group classes; confusable Class A versus B versus C.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A04
Commercial drivers must pass additional knowledge and skills tests described in the separate Commercial Driver's License Handbook. [A04]
Why it matters: group classes; scope note commercial.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A05
The F endorsement is a commercial-license exemption for firefighters operating fire equipment, for military members driving military vehicles on active duty, and for farm employees or family hauling supplies within 150 miles of the farm unless they are a common or contract carrier or carry placarded hazardous materials. [A05]
Why it matters: group endorsements; difficulty high.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A05
A commercial motor vehicle is one used in commerce with a weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, or designed for 16 or more people including the driver, or carrying hazardous materials. [A05]
Why it matters: group classes; scope note commercial.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A06
A motorcycle permit issued between 15½ and 18 lasts one year, but one issued after age 17 expires on the 18th birthday; at 18 or older it lasts six months and can be renewed only once every five years. [A06]
Why it matters: group motorcycle; scope note motorcycle only.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A06
Passing an approved motorcycle safety course may replace the motorcycle tests, but failing the DMV motorcycle skills test two or more times permanently bars future motorcycle permits (NRS 483.280). [A06]
Why it matters: group motorcycle; scope note motorcycle only.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A06
A motorcycle license requires age 16, a vision test, the general and motorcycle knowledge tests and the Motorcycle Operators Skills Test, and riders must wear a helmet. [A06]
Why it matters: group motorcycle; scope note motorcycle only.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A07
A restricted license is a special-circumstance exception: drivers of 14 or 15 qualify only with family hardship or a school-travel need, and others only after serving half of a suspension or revocation. [A07]
Why it matters: group licenses; confusable restricted license versus permit.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A08
A lost, stolen or illegible license should be replaced immediately with a duplicate, online or in person, and the DMV may use the record and photo already on file. [A08]
Why it matters: group records; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A08
An ID card based on limited-term immigration documents expires on the departure date, or one year after issuance when no date is listed. [A08]
Why it matters: group ID cards; confusable standard versus limited-term expiry.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A08
An honorably discharged veteran can add a veteran designation at an initial or renewal license or ID by bringing proof of honorable discharge and signing a release to the Nevada Department of Veterans Services. [A08]
Why it matters: group designations; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A08
An optional medical indicator, shown as a recognized medical symbol on the front of the card, needs a completed Confidential Physician Report (DMV Form DLD-7) naming one listed medical code. [A08]
Why it matters: group designations; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A09
The DMV takes contributions for the Anatomical Gift Account during licensing and through Organ Donor license plates, and gifts of $1 or more to the Gift of Life Education Fund go to the University of Nevada School of Medicine. [A09]
Why it matters: group donation; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A10
Possible signs of sex trafficking include not knowing one's whereabouts, not holding one's own ID or passport, controlled communication and a fearful or submissive manner, and a suspected trafficker should never be confronted. [A10]
Why it matters: group public safety; difficulty low.
Source: [A10 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R22 | anchor: A11
Drivers 65 and older pay $17.25 for an original, duplicate, renewal or instruction permit, and ID cards for ages 10 to 17 cost $9.25. [A11]
Why it matters: group fees; confusable age-based fees.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R23 | anchor: A11
A change of address alone costs $3.25, and each knowledge and skills retest costs $10 after the $25 initial test fee. [A11]
Why it matters: group fees; difficulty low.
Source: [A11 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R24 | anchor: A12
Reinstating a commercial license also requires paying a non-CDL reinstatement fee. [A12]
Why it matters: group fees; scope note commercial.
Source: [A12 -> pdf-0024]
